chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

We were in al-Madinah after the passing of Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), I and Sahib al-Taq, while the people had gathered around Abdullah ibn Ja'far, considering him the holder of the authority after his father. So we entered upon him, I and Sahib al-Taq, while the people were with him. That was because they had narrated from Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام) that he said: the matter is with the eldest so long as there is no defect in him.

We entered upon him asking him about what we used to ask his father. So we asked him about zakat, on how much it becomes obligatory. He said: on two hundred, five. We said: then on one hundred? He said: two dirhams and a half. We said: by Allah, the Murji'ah do not even say this. He raised his hand toward the sky and said: by Allah, I do not know what the Murji'ah say.

He said: so we left his presence astray, not knowing where to turn, I and Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal. We sat in one of the alleys of al-Madinah, weeping and bewildered, not knowing where to turn or whom to seek. We were saying: to the Murji'ah? to the Qadariyyah? to the Zaydiyyah? to the Mu'tazilah? to the Khawarij? While we were in that state, I saw an old man whom I did not know, gesturing to me with his hand. I feared that he might be one of the spies of Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, for he had spies in al-Madinah watching to see whom the Shi'ah of Ja'far (عليه السلام) agreed upon, so that they might strike his neck. So I feared he was one of them.

So I said to al-Ahwal: move away, for I fear for myself and for you. He only intends me and not you, so move away from me lest you perish and help against yourself. So he moved aside, not far away, and I followed the old man, for I thought that I would not be able to escape him. I continued following him, having resolved myself to death, until he brought me to the door of Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام). Then he left me and went away. There was a servant at the door who said to me: enter, may Allah have mercy on you.

So I entered, and there was Abu al-Hasan Musa (عليه السلام). He said to me, initiating the speech: not to the Murji'ah, nor to the Qadariyyah, nor to the Zaydiyyah, nor to the Mu'tazilah, nor to the Khawarij; to me, to me. I said: may I be your ransom, your father has passed away? He said: yes. I said: has he passed away in death? He said: yes. I said: then who is for us after him? He said: if Allah wills to guide you, He will guide you. I said: may I be your ransom, Abdullah claims that he is after his father. He said: Abdullah wants that Allah not be worshipped.

He said: I said, may I be your ransom, then who is for us after him? He said: if Allah wills to guide you, He will guide you. He said: I said, may I be your ransom, so are you he? He said: no, I do not say that. He said: so I said within myself, I have not asked in the right way. Then I said to him: may I be your ransom, is there an Imam over you? He said: no.

Then there entered into me something that none knows but Allah, Mighty and Majestic: a magnification of him and awe greater than what used to come over me from his father when I entered upon him. Then I said to him: may I be your ransom, may I ask you about what I used to ask your father? He said: ask, you will be informed, but do not disclose it, for if you disclose it, then it is slaughter. So I asked him, and behold, he was an ocean that is not exhausted.

I said: may I be your ransom, your Shi'ah and the Shi'ah of your father are astray; may I convey to them and call them to you, while you have taken confidentiality from me? He said: whoever you sense maturity in, then convey to him, and take from him confidentiality; for if they disclose it, then it is slaughter. And he gestured with his hand to his throat.

He said: so I came out from his presence and met Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal. He said to me: what news do you have? I said: guidance. So I told him the story. Then we met al-Fudayl and Abu Basir, and they entered upon him, heard his words, questioned him, and became certain of his Imamate. Then we met the people in groups; everyone who entered upon him became certain, except for the group of Ammar and his companions. Abdullah remained, with only a few people entering upon him. When he saw that, he said: what is the matter with the people? He was informed that Hisham had turned the people away from you. Hisham said: more than one man was stationed for me in al-Madinah to strike me.

key_terms.الذَّبْحُ: slaughter; a warning of lethal political persecution if the matter were disclosed
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat (alms-tax), used here as a test question in jurisprudence
key_terms.الْأَمْرِ: the divinely designated authority and leadership of the Imamate
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةِ: the office of the Imam as rightful divine leadership
key_terms.الْكِتْمَانَ: concealment and confidentiality regarding the Imam's identity under danger
key_terms.الْمُرْجِئَةِ: the Murji'ah, mentioned as one of the sectarian groups contrasted with the path of the Imam
key_terms.الْهُدَى: guidance; the narrator's description of finding the true Imam
key_terms.بَحْرٌ لَا يُنْزَفُ: an inexhaustible ocean; describing the Imam's limitless knowledge

ai.seo_question: How did the companions recognize the Imamate of Imam Musa al-Kazim (عليه السلام) after Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how Hisham ibn Salim and others were left confused after the martyrdom of Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) and tested the claim of Abdullah ibn Ja'far, only to find him unable to answer basic questions correctly. They were then guided to Imam Musa al-Kazim (عليه السلام), whose knowledge, spiritual authority, and instruction established his Imamate for them, while also emphasizing secrecy due to political danger.
